questions.heading: The Snapshot Covers the Inputs, and Nothing About Who or When
questions.stem: scenario_record.py asks load_portfolio for a portfolio whose seed differs from the one behind the base scenario's recorded hash. What did the program print after 'refused:'?

options.text: portfolio medium/2027 does not match the hash the scenario recorded
options.says: The program printed 'refused: portfolio small/2028 does not match the hash the scenario recorded'; it asked for the small portfolio with seed 2028.

options.text: portfolio small/2027 does not match the hash the scenario recorded
options.says: 2027 is the default seed the recorded hash belongs to; the program asked for seed 2028 and printed 'portfolio small/2028'.

options.text: portfolio medium/2028 does not match the hash the scenario recorded
options.says: The base scenario is on the small portfolio; the printed line is 'refused: portfolio small/2028 does not match the hash the scenario recorded'.

options.text: portfolio small/2028 does not match the hash the scenario recorded
options.says: Right: the program asked for seed 2028 while the recorded hash belongs to seed 2027, so load_portfolio refused small/2028 before any model was built.

questions.heading: A Copy Shares Nothing Mutable With Its Parent
questions.stem: A service copies a scenario with copy.copy, gives the copy a new id, and a planner then lowers one year's budget in the copy. What happens to the original scenario?

options.text: The original's budget changes too, since both hold one budget dictionary
options.says: Right: a shallow copy shares the budget dictionary ('same dict object: True').

options.text: The original's budget stays, since copy.copy also copies the budget dict
options.says: copy.copy is shallow; the program printed 'same dict object: True' and base 2030 = 7750.

options.text: The original's budget stays, since the new id gives the copy its own fields
options.says: Fields of a shallow copy point at the same inner objects; the id is a separate field.

options.text: The original's budget changes, but its snapshot keeps its first value
options.says: The snapshot is recomputed from the inputs: 'base snapshot changed: True'.

questions.heading: Optimize Builds the Model From the Scenario and Stamps the Result With Its Snapshot
questions.stem: optimize_scenarios.py solves the base scenario S-001 and its copy S-002, whose 2030 budget is cut from $8,610k to $7,750k, before a 2031 edit leaves the S-002 result stale. What NPVs did it print for the two solves?

options.says: The program printed 'S-001 OPTIMAL NPV $24,260k'; the base solved to $24,260k.
The program printed 'S-002 OPTIMAL NPV $23,887k'; the cut costs $373k ($24,260k less $23,887k).
Right: 'S-001 OPTIMAL NPV $24,260k' and 'S-002 OPTIMAL NPV $23,887k', so the $860k cut costs $373k of NPV.
Neither matches: the program printed 'S-001 OPTIMAL NPV $24,260k' and 'S-002 OPTIMAL NPV $23,887k'.
